summary: Rudolf Much was a scholar in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1883–1887), where he later held an academic post from circa 1895 to 1934.

Rudolf Otto worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1888–1891) and under Richard von Garbe, later holding posts at the University of Breslau (~1914–1917) and the University of Marburg (~1917–1937).
Rudolf Seydel worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1853–1857) and subsequently held a post there from circa 1860 to 1892.

Rudolf Thurneysen was a linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig (~1876–1879) and under Heinrich Zimmer (~1878–1879). He held posts at the University of Jena (~1882–1887), University of Freiburg (~1898–1913), and University of Bonn (~1913–1923).

Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Evangelisches Stift Tübingen (~1839–1843) under Heinrich Ewald and under Eugène Burnouf (~1843–1844). He held posts at the University of Tübingen as Privatdozent (1845) and Extraordinarius (1848–1895).

Rudrapatna Shamasastry was an Indologist who completed degrees at the University of Madras, Government Sanskrit College, Mysore, Oriental University, and University of Calcutta. He was Principal at Sri Chamarajendra Samskrita Maha Patashala (1912–1918) and Curator at Oriental Research Institute Mysore (1918–1929).

Ruixuan Chen works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leiden University (PhD attested 2018) under Paul Harrison, Jens-Uwe Hartmann, Adelheid Mette, Olav Hackstein, and Helmut Tauscher. He is attested at Peking University (2026).

Rulon Wells worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah (~1935–1939) and Harvard University (~1939–1942), and held a long-term post at Yale University from circa 1945 to 1989.

Rupert Gethin specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Manchester (~1977–1987) under Lance S. Cousins. His career includes posts at the University of Bristol (1987; 2009–2023) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2026).

Ruriko Sakuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Nagoya University. She held posts at Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2015, 2026), International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2026), and International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Ruth Fuller Sasaki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Chicago (1927–1929) and under teachers including D. T. Suzuki, Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki, Mukai Kono, and Zuigan Goto. She directed the First Zen Institute of America (~1945–1967).

Ruth Gamble works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the Australian National University (-2014) supervised by John Powers, Roger R. Jackson, and David Templeman, later holding research posts at ANU and the University of Munich (attested 2016).

Ryan Anningson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed studies at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2017) under the supervision of Jason Neelis.

Ryan Richard Overbey specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Brown University (-2001) and Harvard University (-2010), later holding posts at UC Berkeley (2013–2015), Wesleyan University (attested 2016), Holy Cross, and Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Ryo Nishimura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Tohoku University from circa 1991 to 1995 and under Fumihiko Sueki from circa 1996 to 2004.
Ryodo Kudo is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has held academic teaching appointments at Taisho University (attested 2015–2026) and Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

Ryoen Minamoto was a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1947–1952), he held posts at Japan Women's University (~1964–1972), International Christian University (~1984–1991), and Tohoku University (Emeritus Professor ~1984–2020).

Ryogon Fukuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1931–1936) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1938–1941). He taught at Humboldt University of Berlin and held a professorship at Ryukoku University (~1960–1980).
Ryoichi Kondo is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He has held posts as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

Ryoji Kishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held appointments at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).
